Wilderness of En-gedi
en-GEH-dee
proper noun
Hebrew midbar En-gedi, “fountain of the kid”; the desert of crags and caves by the western shore of the salt sea.

Biblical Definition

By the springs of En-gedi, where fresh water leaps down cliffs above the salt and lifeless sea, lies a labyrinth of caves among the rocks of the wild goats. When Saul was returned from following the Philistines, they told him David was in the wilderness of En-gedi (1Sa 24:1), and he took three thousand chosen men and went to seek him upon the rocks. There, in the very cave where David and his men lay hid, Saul came in to cover his feet; and David’s men whispered that God had delivered his enemy into his hand. But David only cut off the skirt of Saul’s robe, and his heart smote him even for that, saying, The LORD forbid that I should do this thing unto my master, the LORD’s anointed. He would not stretch forth his hand, but committed his cause to God: The LORD judge between me and thee, and the LORD avenge me of thee: but mine hand shall not be upon thee. Here is a lesson the flesh never learns of itself: vengeance belongeth to the LORD, and the man after God’s heart will not seize by violence what God hath promised to give in His time. In this restraint David foreshadowed a greater Son of David, who, when He was reviled, reviled not again, but committed Himself to Him that judgeth righteously. The caves of En-gedi preach the patience of the anointed who waiteth on God.

Webster 1828 Definition

The desert of caves and springs by the salt sea where David spared Saul’s life (1Sa 24:1); a witness that vengeance belongs to the LORD, and a figure of Christ who committed Himself to Him that judgeth righteously.

WILDERNESS OF EN-GEDI, the rocky desert by the springs of En-gedi on the salt sea.

Saul sought David there with three thousand chosen men (1Sa 24:1).

In a cave David cut Saul’s skirt but would not touch the LORD’s anointed.

The LORD judge between me and thee: David left vengeance to God.

A figure of Christ, who reviled not again but committed Himself to a righteous Judge.

Key Scripture

Isa 32:2 — "And a man shall be as an hiding place from the wind, and a covert from the tempest; as rivers of water in a dry place, as the shadow of a great rock in a weary land."

Psa 46:1 — "To the chief Musician for the sons of Korah, A Song upon Alamoth. God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble."

Isa 43:2 — "When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee."

Psa 63:1 — "A Psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah. O God, thou art my God; early will I seek thee: my soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is;"

Modern Corruption

No modern redefinition attends this desert; the truth to recover is that vengeance is the LORD’s, and the godly wait for God to right their wrongs.

expand to see more

The wilderness of En-gedi with its springs and caves is a real place above the salt sea, and David’s forbearance is written for our learning.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the believer must not avenge himself, but give place unto wrath, for the LORD hath said, Vengeance is mine, I will repay. David had the king in his hand and would not strike, because Saul was the LORD’s anointed and the throne was God’s to give. So the Christian, wronged and pursued, commits his cause to the righteous Judge, and waits, as his Master waited upon the cross.

Hebrew Roots

En-gedi, “fountain of the kid,” from the springs where wild goats water among the crags; the surrounding desert bears the name.

expand to see more

En-gedi — Hebrew En-gedi, “fountain (or spring) of the kid.”

Ayin, a fountain or eye; gedi, a kid or young goat.

Midbar, wilderness, the rocky waste enclosing the springs.

The rocks of the wild goats nearby (1Sa 24:2) give the place its character.

Distinct from the town and vineyards of En-gedi, treated in their own entry.

Usage

"They told Saul, David is in the wilderness of En-gedi."

"In a cave of En-gedi David spared the LORD’s anointed."

"The wilderness of En-gedi teaches that vengeance belongs to the LORD."
